evidence.text: AERO's 3Q26 guide (op margin 14-17%, adj EBITDAR 26.5-29.5%) was built on $3.2/gal all-in fuel. Peers guiding the same week used higher numbers: United $3.69 all-in (July 14 curve), Volaris $3.50 Gulf Coast. Delta then realised $3.80 GAAP / $3.61 adjusted in Q3 and absorbed $500m+ more fuel than its July forecast. AERO paid $4.20 in Q2, close to United's $4.19, so its Q3 fuel was likely around $3.8-4.0, about $0.6-0.8/gal (~$70-95m, ~5pp of margin on ~$1.6bn revenue) above its own assumption before recapture. Reported operating margin will likely land below the 14-17% guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: op margin 4.6% landed at the low end of the 4-7% guide on $4.20 fuel and EPS -$0.40 missed -$0.37; the stock rose +2.29% the next session (baseline 2026-07-13 amc). Q1: margin at the low end of guide, about -4.9%. The holders have looked through fuel-driven margin misses before.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The CEO wrote 'higher jet fuel prices continue to create a more challenging cost environment than anticipated' in the September traffic release, and Delta's fuel miss was public on 10-09. If no one had priced it, the EPS estimates would cluster near last year's $1.2; they range $0.24-0.61. What may be unpriced is how far below peers AERO's $3.2 assumption sat: a model that haircut the guide by a peer-sized fuel gap would still be too high.
evidence.independence: Delta Q3 8-K, 2026-10-09 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000027904/000002790426000035/deltaairlinesannouncessept.htm); United Q2 8-K Q3 fuel assumption (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm); Volaris Q2 guide (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/controladora-vuela-compania-de-aviacion-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-22/); AERO September traffic CEO quote (https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results). Shares the July 6-K with the Q4 guide finding, but this one is the Q3 line and that one is the Q4/FY line.

evidence.text: AERO's 4Q26 guide (op margin 15.5-18.5%, EBITDAR 28-31%) and FY26 guide (op margin 11-13%, EBITDAR 24-26%) assume $3.0/gal. The forward curve has moved far above that: Delta's 4Q guide uses the 2026-10-02 curve, about $4.25 all-in after a ~$0.40 refinery benefit; NY jet hit $4.95 on 2026-10-10 (Bloomberg via aggregator); Gulf Coast peaked at $4.705 on Sept 15. With ~125m Q4 gallons, a $1.2-1.5/gal gap is ~$150-190m, about 9-11pp of Q4 margin before recapture. The peso also weakened to 17.97 by 30 September against a 17.6 Q4 assumption. A large Q4/FY guide cut is near-certain on the 20 October call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No confirmed AERO reaction to a guide cut since the November 2025 IPO. Q1 2026, when FY guidance was withdrawn and Q2 was guided to 4-7%, drew about -4.9%. Closest peer analog: Delta cut FY EPS from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60 on fuel on 2026-10-09 and fell about 3%, inside its ~4% implied move (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx).
evidence.why_not_priced: The direction is priced: the stock is 30% off its high and the fuel curve is public. The size may not be. AERO's $3.0 Q4 assumption sits further below the curve than US peers' assumptions did, AERO has no refinery offset, and it already ran a 4.6% op margin in a $4.20 quarter. If the cut were fully priced, AERO would have fallen when Delta cut on 10-09 and jet set new highs on 10-10; instead it is flat over 20 days.
evidence.independence: Jet price path: GlobalAir/Flycraft Gulf Coast spot (https://www.flycraft.com/jet-fuel-price); Bloomberg via aggregator on Oct 10 highs (https://stockhub.kr/en/news/news_f45cea4bff87); peso at 17.97 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.eldolar.info/es-MX/mexico/dia/20260930). Applied to AGNC's $8.58 June TBV, a peer-like quarter means roughly $7.2-7.5 at 9/30.

AGNC fell ~13% over the week of its preliminary results (https://www.fool.com/investing/2023/10/26/why-agnc-investment-stock-dropped-13-this-week). In the 8 baseline prints, all in quieter book quarters, |move| has a median of 1.41% and 6 of 8 were up.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. If the market had not priced it, AGNC would still trade near its $8.95 Oct 1 close at a premium to June TBV. Instead it is -15.5% over 20 days at $8.42, and four brokers cut targets after these releases. What remains open is whether AGNC's own decline matches the peers, since AGNC has historically shown lower book beta than ORC.
evidence.independence: IVR's own 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000076/ivr10142026-8kxex991.htm, 2026-10-14) is a separate company and document. evidence.text: AGNC went into Q3 deliberately long duration. Its duration gap was +0.7 years at 6/30, and management said on the Q2 call it 'prefers a positive duration gap'. The Q2 10-Q sensitivity, as summarised by an AI-generated page and not yet verified against the 10-Q itself, puts +75bp in rates at -8.8% of TBV. The 10-year then rose ~85bp in the quarter (4.42% on 6/30 to multidecade highs above 5.2% by late September), the biggest quarterly rise since 2016. AGNC's own positioning therefore points to a book decline at least as large as the peers', before any MBS spread widening.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q2 call, TBV +2.4% for the quarter but about -1% QTD in July, and the stock moved -1.28% (baseline 2026-07-20). In Q3 2023, a large rate-driven TBV loss plus a negative QTD update coincided with a ~13% weekly drop.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Sell-side models carry the duration gap. If the market had fully priced a worse-than-peer book, AGNC would not still be the most expensive agency mREIT on price to book (1.11x per Insider Monkey on Oct 15). The premium suggests the market still credits AGNC with better book protection than ORC and IVR, which its stated rate positioning does not support in a +85bp quarter.
evidence.independence: The sensitivity figure comes from https://www.panabee.com/news/agnc-investment-earnings-q2-2026-report, an AI-generated summary of the Q2 10-Q that also gives the 0.7-year gap; it shares the company as source. The rate move is independent: Morningstar/Dow Jones has 4.420% on 2026-06-30 (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202606307321/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4420-data-talk), and a WSJ quarter summary (via search) has +85bp for the quarter.

evidence.text: October quarter-to-date conditions for the call's TBV update are mixed to negative. The 10-year eased from its Oct 6-7 peak of 5.31% to 5.06-5.15% (Mortgage News Daily). But Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rate rose from 7.28% (Oct 1) to 7.40% (Oct 8 and Oct 15), which suggests the mortgage-to-Treasury spread widened further in October rather than retracing. AGNC stock is about -6% since its $8.95 Oct 1 close.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: AGNC customarily gives a QTD TBV figure on the call. July 2026: ~-1%, and the stock moved -1.28%. October 2023: ~-11% QTD, and the stock fell ~13% over the week. April 2025: an intra-quarter update of -5.5% (to $7.80) came during a broad rally, and the stock moved +2.83% (baseline 2025-04-10).
evidence.why_not_priced: Only partly priced. The market can see rates and an AGNC price that is down about 6% in October, but has no company number for October. A flat or positive QTD figure would be a relief; a further -3% to -5% would extend the de-rating. The stock's -3% fall on the print day suggests holders lean toward the bad case.
evidence.independence: Freddie Mac series via Trading Economics (https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/30-year-mortgage-rate/news/588887, 2026-10-01, with the Oct 8 and Oct 15 updates). Primary mortgage rates are a lagging proxy for secondary MBS spreads, so this is a proxy and not company data.

evidence.text: Wider spreads raise AGNC's forward returns, and the dividend has just been reaffirmed. On the Q2 call management said 15-17% ROEs on 130-150bp spreads at 7-7.5x leverage 'align really well' with the $0.12 monthly dividend. It also said the GSEs, with ~$120bn of purchase capacity, would buy aggressively at 160-170bp. Spreads have since widened 'well above the year-to-date average' (Guggenheim), Pulte said on Sep 18 that the GSEs are buying 'large quantities', and AGNC declared the October $0.12 dividend on Oct 7-8. The call is likely to present wider spreads as a higher-ROE entry point and to reaffirm the dividend.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2025: after a -5.5% intra-quarter book hit, the Q1 2025 print moved +3.55% (baseline 2025-04-21) as management pointed to wide-spread returns. Over the 8 baseline prints, 6 were up.
evidence.why_not_priced: A 16.5% dividend yield and a 52-week low price in a dividend-cut risk. Had the market priced a dividend reaffirmed on better forward ROE, the stock would not have fallen 3% into the print, and BofA and JPM would not have cut targets to $8-8.50 on Oct 16.

evidence.text: AGNC carries the highest price-to-book among the mortgage REITs Insider Monkey compared: 1.11x on the Oct 13 close of $8.61, against 0.76-1.05 for the others. A confirmed double-digit TBV decline therefore leaves the premium exposed to compression on the print.

evidence.why_not_priced: The book basis behind the 1.11x is not stated (it implies about $7.76). If the market had already marked AGNC to a peer-like ~$7.3 book, the premium would sit near 1.15x. That is high for a quarter of book loss, and its persistence suggests the market credits AGNC's franchise more than a confirmed number may support.
evidence.independence: This shares its underlying concern with findings 1 and 2 (the size of the TBV hit), but the fact is different: the valuation premium, not the book change. No independent source for the peer P/B figures.

evidence.text: GM's July guide 'assumes no material Middle East escalation'. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: GM's CFO played down gas-price demand effects in Q1 2026 and Barra said the shift to smaller vehicles 'is just not happening' on the Q2 call. The stock rose on both prints, so this line has not yet cost GM a reaction.

GPC also said June NAPA sales were roughly flat because of higher fuel prices, and it cut the Automotive outlook on consumer sentiment.
